name: Talassemtane National Park
hero_subtitle: Fir forests, limestone peaks and long trails in the heart of the Rif Mountains.

overview.title: Wild Country Behind the Blue Town
overview.p1: Talassemtane National Park was created in 2004 to protect a large area of the Rif Mountains, home to rare Moroccan fir forests, limestone cliffs, streams and small mountain villages. It is one of the greenest, most dramatic landscapes in northern Morocco.
overview.p2: Most visitors come for a day hike, often through Akchour, but longer trekking routes cross the park too. Trails can be steep and poorly marked, and the weather changes fast, so go with a local guide for anything beyond the main routes, and tell someone your plan. Spring and early autumn are the best seasons.

tips.title: Practical Tips for Visiting Talassemtane National Park

1.title: Getting There
1.desc: Reach the park from Chefchaouen by grand taxi, private driver or an organised tour. Akchour is about 45 minutes away.

2.title: Timing
2.desc: Go in spring or early autumn. Winters can be cold and wet, and trails may be slippery after rain.

3.title: Good to Know
3.desc: Hire a local guide for longer routes, carry plenty of water and tell someone your plan. Phone signal can be patchy.

q1.question: Where is Talassemtane National Park?
q1.answer: In the Rif Mountains in northern Morocco, around and beyond Chefchaouen. Akchour is a popular gateway.

q2.question: Do I need a guide for Talassemtane?
q2.answer: For popular routes like Akchour, not always. For longer or remote trails, a local guide is strongly advised.

q3.question: What is the best time to visit the park?
q3.answer: Spring for greenery and water, or early autumn for warm, settled days.

q4.question: Can I visit the park without a car?
q4.answer: Yes. Grand taxis and organised tours run from Chefchaouen to the main trailheads like Akchour.
